findings.title: Role changes leave the previous authorization cached for up to 60 seconds

evidence.observation: Role is updated, but invalidateIdentityCache is called only for active === false.
Same role write and deactivation-only invalidation in SQLite twin.
Identity cache TTL is 60,000 ms and valid cached role returns before reading DB.
Request authorization role comes from resolved identity; no separate fresh role lookup.

findings.expected_behavior: A successful demotion must remove previous privileges on subsequent authorization checks.
findings.actual_behavior: Source-confirmed: a previously cached admin/accountant identity survives a role-only update until cache expiry. No live unauthorized write was performed.
findings.root_cause: The mutation and authorization cache have no invalidation contract for role/name changes.
reproduction_steps: On isolated DB, authenticate target as admin/accountant and call a privileged endpoint to warm cache.
As another admin, PATCH target role to viewer.
Before 60 seconds, reuse original token on a privileged endpoint and compare current DB role.
findings.potential_impact: A demoted account can retain elevated authorization for the remainder of the 60-second cache window on a warmed process. Other processes need independent invalidation or fresh reads.
missing_tests: Warm real identity cache; demote through route; immediately verify old JWT is denied at privileged route on both engines and each replica.
findings.recommended_fix: Invalidate cached identity after every authorization-affecting committed update; define multi-process revocation propagation/fresh-read policy.
regression_risks: Transaction rollback must not publish an incorrect cache state; role grants/name updates and replica invalidation need coverage.
blocking_conditions: Database/Express runtime not available; source reasoning only, live sequence pending.

findings.title: User mutations and their durable sync records do not commit atomically

evidence.observation: update resolves before snapshot and enqueue; an enqueue failure returns 500 after the write.
deactivation also precedes snapshot/enqueue.
runWithTenantContext only invokes AsyncLocalStorage.run; it is not a transaction.
userRepo takes raw db while outbox takes ambient dbx.
Invitation consume finishes before created-user snapshot is enqueued.

findings.expected_behavior: User state and its outbox event must commit together, with retries preserving the same result.
findings.actual_behavior: Source-confirmed: user update/deactivation/password reset (and invitation-created user enqueue) run as separate persistence steps; failure between them can leave committed user state absent from outbox.
findings.root_cause: Route lacks a shared committing transaction; user repository is wired to raw DB and uses tenant context, while outbox is a separate call.
reproduction_steps: Use synthetic isolated tenant/device/user.
Make outbox enqueue fail after user UPDATE.
Observe HTTP failure, query users and outbox, restart sync and compare peer state.
findings.potential_impact: Peer devices may retain stale role, credentials or active state. HTTP failure can conceal a successful local write; invitation retry may encounter an already-consumed code. Failure and two-device divergence not executed.
missing_tests: Inject snapshot and outbox failures after each mutation on PG/SQLite; assert rollback or durable retry record; verify peer user state after restart.
findings.recommended_fix: Make user write, session/device changes and outbox share one transaction and a transaction-aware user repository. Invitation consumption must include durable user event before commitment.
regression_risks: Simply wrapping the route is insufficient if raw DB ignores ambient transaction; maintain RLS, rollback safety and idempotency.
blocking_conditions: No isolated DB or two-device stack; failure injection not executed.

findings.title: Invitation controls have visible labels without programmatic associations

findings.expected_behavior: Each invitation control should expose its visible field label as the associated accessible label.
findings.actual_behavior: Source confirms no association for five controls; particularly name and TTL have neither an associated label nor explicit accessible name. Browser accessibility tree not inspected.
findings.root_cause: InvitationManager uses raw sibling Label/Input/Select while FormField provides association elsewhere.
reproduction_steps: In prepared browser open settings/users and inspect generated label for/id relationships.
Query controls by displayed label and click name/TTL labels to check focus.
findings.potential_impact: Assistive technology cannot reliably identify fields by their displayed purpose; label click will not focus sibling input.

findings.recommended_fix: Use stable htmlFor/id or the existing FormField association; wire SelectTrigger explicitly.
regression_risks: Retain RTL layout and unique IDs when multiple dialogs/managers exist.
blocking_conditions: Browser/component dependencies absent; source confirmation only.

findings.title: Dashboard development proxy can forward remote callers into passwordless loopback licensing administration

evidence.observation: host:true exposes dev proxy on all interfaces; /license-admin forwards to loopback license server by default.
openLoopback defaults on outside production unless explicitly disabled; binding helper restricts only backend listener.
Any loopback socket is accepted as super_admin without credential even if req.ip is remote.
Actual transformed middleware with synthetic remote req.ip + loopback socket calls next with super_admin; remote socket and closed-loopback controls return 401.

findings.expected_behavior: A network-accessible proxy must not confer the local owner bypass on unauthenticated remote requests.
findings.actual_behavior: Middleware policy reproduced in memory; configured proxy creates the required socket origin by source analysis. Live Vite→license-server→DB path and network reachability not reproduced.
findings.root_cause: Backend trusts proxy socket loopback while frontend dev server accepts non-loopback clients.
reproduction_steps: In a disposable prepared stack use default dev dashboard/license server, no real license data.
From controlled second network context send unauthenticated GET to dashboard /license-admin/licenses.
Verify request is rejected rather than returning synthetic license data; then test authorized controls.
findings.potential_impact: If both development services run with defaults on the same machine and port 5174 is reachable, unauthenticated remote clients may read or control licensing through the proxy. Production default disables openLoopback; no unconditional production exposure claimed.
missing_tests: Real local Vite proxy with isolated licensing DB: remote-client-shaped unauthenticated requests denied; local owner path still meets intended policy.
findings.recommended_fix: Bind owner dashboard to loopback or require authenticated backend admin requests across proxy; constrain bypass to a verifiable local-only boundary.
regression_risks: Preserve intended owner console and automation tokens; forwarded IP trust alone cannot override current socket OR check.
blocking_conditions: Dependencies unavailable; live proxy integration and external reachability unverified. No remote systems contacted.

findById tries payments first and falls back to receipt only on not-found.

Edit hydration exits when editing.kind differs from form kind.
Actual adapter/entity returned payment/supplier for synthetic receipt/customer DTO; receipt fallback never called.

findings.actual_behavior: Adapter defect reproduced with mocked server response consistent with source: receipt becomes payment/supplier. Receipt edit hydration is then rejected by source guard. No live browser/API test run.
findings.root_cause: Client assumes /payments/:id filters by kind while server aliases are generic by ID. Mapper trusts endpoint name and overwrites DTO kind.
reproduction_steps: On isolated stack create a receipt, open edit from receipts list.

findings.title: Voucher and return cancellation always throw after the backend cancellation succeeds
findings.category: Failure propagation / financial and inventory UI
findings.symbol: cancelByReference and its two use-case callers

evidence.observation: cancelByReference unconditionally throws Ledger cancellation is performed by domain use cases.
Awaits voucher cancel, then calls throwing ledger cancellation.
Awaits return cancel, then same throwing call.
Production container connects both use cases to the ApiLedgerRepository instance (declared at line144).
Stock/query/financial invalidation occurs only onSuccess; rejection instead triggers failure toast.
Actual use cases with actual ledger adapter rejected after both synthetic document cancellation operations succeeded.

findings.expected_behavior: Successful backend cancellation should resolve successfully, refresh affected views, and allow amendment continuation. Backend owns financial and stock reversal.
findings.actual_behavior: Both use cases always reject after a successful document cancellation when wired to actual API ledger adapter. Hook success invalidation is skipped; voucher amend aborts before replacement creation.
findings.root_cause: Frontend use cases still attempt an extra ledger cancellation although API adapter explicitly refuses it and backend cancellation already owns that side effect.
reproduction_steps: In prepared isolated stack cancel active receipt/payment/return via UI.
Compare failure toast and cached status with persisted cancelled document, ledger and inventory.
Current bounded reproduction CHECK-101 proves both caller/adapter sequences without DB.
findings.potential_impact: Users see cancellation failure while backend has cancelled a financial/stock document; stale balances/stock and retries mislead operators. Voucher amendment cancels original but never reaches replacement creation. Backend DB effects traced by source, not executed.
missing_tests: Use actual API ledger adapter with real use-case wiring; assert cancellation resolves and invalidates all consumers. Integration DB checks should verify single reversal and repeat safety.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove redundant client ledger cancellation from API-backed document cancellation orchestration, following current CancelInvoiceUseCase ownership; retain authoritative backend reversal and test actual container wiring.
regression_risks: Mocks currently assert extra ledger call; update tests to business outcome without weakening backend reversal checks. Amendment still needs atomic replacement (ERP-008).
blocking_conditions: Live persistence/cross-screen checks require safe installed stack; current reproduction uses synthetic successful document repositories.

findings.title: Voucher amendment has no transaction spanning cancellation and replacement

evidence.observation: save awaits cancellation before independent create; catch does not restore original.
Create and cancel are separate POST operations.
Creation has its own transaction; cancellation routes have separate transactions, no replace operation.
Cancel changes ledger status and reverses invoice paid before create request can begin.

findings.expected_behavior: An amendment either commits a replacement together with cancellation or preserves original financial effect on failure.
findings.actual_behavior: Confirmed source design: cancellation commits before replacement validation/network/DB persistence. Currently ERP-007 deterministically aborts even earlier; after that issue is fixed, independent create failure still leaves original cancelled. This is a separate transaction-design cause, not a second count of ERP-007 runtime symptom.
findings.root_cause: Two standalone HTTP mutations implement one business amendment without transactional replacement or durable recovery orchestration.
reproduction_steps: After accounting for ERP-007, use isolated payment edit and inject create failure following successful cancel.
A notes value exceeding schema max2000 is one candidate late-validation case; do not treat as executed.
Assert original remains active or replacement and reversal commit together; test crash/disconnect between operations.
findings.potential_impact: A rejected or interrupted correction removes the original financial effect without recording the replacement. Separate sync events can also expose intermediate cancelled state.
missing_tests: Both-engine atomic replace; invalid input, stale expectedVersion, insufficient data, outbox failure and lost response; idempotent retry; peer convergence.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement one idempotent version-checked backend replace operation covering cancel+create+ledger+outbox, validating replacement before committing either side.
regression_risks: Document numbering, reference history, consumed advances, day/year locks and retry/version semantics must remain valid. Fixing ERP-007 alone does not close this issue.
blocking_conditions: No installed DB/browser; direct two-request failure/crash test unexecuted; ERP-007 currently interrupts normal UI amend flow.
